intro: Paste the one-page case — the chain, the baseline as it stands today, the threshold with its date set past the trough, the board version in three sentences, and the claim you deliberately left out — plus the reckoning across all six opening positions, in 350–450 words. Resubmission is free and unlimited; the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You are grading the CLOSING submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, CPO / CHRO track — for sitting Chief People Officers and CHROs. Module 6 activity, 'The case', in two parts. PART ONE, a one-page case for a budget holder: (1) the chain worked backwards — business result, then behaviour, then intervention, in that order; (2) the baseline TODAY, an actual number with its source, OR an honest statement that no baseline exists with exactly how they will establish one before anything starts — both are full answers, but an estimate presented as a measurement is not; (3) the threshold — the observation that would tell them to stop, the number, and the date, SET PAST THE J-CURVE with the trough's expected depth stated, so the threshold does not trigger inside the expected decline; (4) the board version in three sentences — what the exposure is and that it is known, who is accountable by name, and the decision rule they are offering to be held to; (5) one impressive figure they could have used and deliberately left out, with the reason. SPECIAL NOTE ON (5): if the learner admits they were tempted by the '28% of AI use cases meet ROI' figure, score that ABOVE a submission that avoided it silently — it is the module's own test, and the figure is scope-laundered (782 infrastructure-and-operations leaders, not HR). A learner who uses that figure as evidence anywhere in their case has failed the module's central test and should be marked down clearly, however good the rest is. PART TWO, the reckoning: the learner committed a position at the start of each of the six modules (personal use on judgment work; calendar weighted to strategic counsel; clarity of AI ownership; consolidation dip and recovery; ability to name every system deciding about people and who reviewed it; ability to give the CEO a defensible number). They must say which moved, what moved them, and whether the movement ran in a CONSISTENT DIRECTION — most people in this seat find their positions were optimistic in one specific way, and naming that pattern is the course's highest-value output. SCORING: grade the account of the change, NEVER the accuracy of any position. A learner whose six positions were all wrong and who can name what they were reading instead of the evidence has done the best work available. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is that a number you cannot baseline today is one you will lose with in eighteen months. Its real counter-argument is that the baseline rule selects for the trivial — the initiatives with clean baselines are the transactional ones Module 2 says are compressing anyway, while the things only a CPO can drive have no clean baseline and never will — plus the sharper version, that demanding thresholds may relocate the dishonesty into thresholds set where they cannot fail. Strong positions say what they would do with the initiative they believe in most if it genuinely cannot produce a falsifiable measure inside a budget cycle.

opening.label: Predicted — how many AI initiatives in your function have a baseline recorded from before they started
opening.hint: Recorded before the initiative began. Zero is a common and honest answer.

calibration.label: Checked — how many actually do, after you looked
calibration.hint: Count only baselines that existed before the work started. One reconstructed afterwards does not count.

dimensions.name: The chain runs backwards from a business result
dimensions.criteria: Business result, then behaviour, then intervention. A learning or adoption objective presented as the business result is the common failure. The result must be something the company wants to be different, stated concretely enough that the CFO would recognize it as their problem rather than the function's.

dimensions.name: The baseline is real, or its absence is honest
dimensions.criteria: An actual current number with its source and ideally its n — or an explicit statement that no baseline exists together with exactly how and by when they will establish one before anything starts. Both score at full credit. An estimate presented as a measurement, or a figure with no source, scores at the bottom: this is the dimension where the module's entire argument is tested, since a threshold without a baseline is unmeasurable by construction.

dimensions.name: The threshold could occur, and is set past the trough
dimensions.criteria: A named observation, a number, and a date, such that a plausible real outcome would trigger it. Then the module's specific requirement: the measurement point set past the expected J-curve trough, with the trough's depth stated. A threshold measured at month three on a service transformation would stop something that was working, and a learner who has not accounted for that has built a mechanism that kills their own initiative on schedule. Also check the threshold is not set where it cannot fail — technically pre-committed and meaningless is the module's own named failure mode.

dimensions.name: The board version does the board's three things
dimensions.criteria: Three sentences: exposure known, accountability by name, and a decision rule offered. Grade whether it would satisfy a director worried about control rather than comprehension. A technology explanation scores at the bottom — the module states plainly that this is the most common failure in that room. Credit a learner who offers Module 5's durable rule as the thing to be held to.

dimensions.name: The omitted claim, and the 28% test
dimensions.criteria: One impressive figure identified and deliberately left out, with the reason. Score ABOVE average any learner who admits they were tempted by the 28% figure and explains why it does not survive the scope question — that is the module's own test and the admission is the point. Mark down clearly any case that USES the 28% figure as evidence about HR, however strong the rest is: the module put that example first specifically so it would be caught here.

dimensions.name: The reckoning finds the direction
dimensions.criteria: All six opening positions revisited: which moved, what moved them, and whether the movement ran in a consistent direction. Grade the account of the change and NEVER the accuracy of any position. The highest-value output is naming the systematic direction of their own optimism — a learner who lists six changes without looking for the pattern has done the arithmetic and missed the finding. Credit heavily a specific account of what they had been reading instead of the evidence when they formed the original position.
